chunks: Whoever was a partner in a male slave or a female slave — little or more — and emancipated his portion, and he has the financial means, let him buy him from his companion and emancipate the whole of him. But if he does not have the financial means from wealth, the slave's value should be assessed on the day he was emancipated, then the slave shall work according to the reckoning of what remains until he is completely emancipated.

key_terms.حِصَّة: One's portion or share of jointly owned property
key_terms.سَعَة: Financial breadth, capability, or leeway; ability to afford something
key_terms.قِيمَة: Assessed monetary value of the slave on a specific day
key_terms.يَسْعَى: To strive/work toward a goal; here the slave working to earn his freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when one co-owner of a slave emancipates his share?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules on the case of a jointly owned slave whose one co-owner emancipates his share. If the emancipating partner is financially able, he must purchase the remaining share from the other co-owner and grant the slave full freedom. If he cannot afford it, the slave works to earn the remaining portion of his value as determined on the day of partial emancipation, thereby gradually earning his complete freedom. This ruling reflects Islamic jurisprudence's preference for complete emancipation over a state of partial bondage.
